---
title: "Web font subsets"
description: "Regenerate and verify committed apps/web font assets without build-time processing."
---

## Scope and behavior

The pilot replaces `next/font` for the web root Noto Sans, marketing Be Vietnam
Pro and JetBrains Mono, and branding Inter and Noto Sans specimens. Other apps
and independent declarations remain unchanged. Public pages and the authenticated
dashboard inherit the same Noto Sans body stack from
`apps/web/src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`; authenticated visual acceptance remains a
merge requirement.

CSS faces share their family before the metric-adjusted fallback. Root Noto Sans
retains `font-display: block`; marketing and branding retain `swap`. Branding
Noto Sans has a separate CSS alias using the same assets and fallback metrics,
so its `swap` does not override the root's `block`. Arial fallback source,
family order, ascent, descent, line gap and size adjustment match the former
Next-generated CSS. CJK continues to use system fallback where these sources
have no glyphs. The original normal faces continue to supply synthetic italics.

Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, full Vietnamese composed characters and supported
combining marks are retained. The core pool contains full Vietnamese coverage.
The original Google character groups retain their shaping priority: a combined
font can change normalization, feature selection and native rendering even when
its glyph outlines and advances match. Noto Sans and Be Vietnam Pro therefore
retain separate Latin and Vietnamese core chunks and their original Latin
Extended data on demand. That Extended face overlaps some Vietnamese characters,
so Vietnamese text can still request it. This is an explicit rendering-preservation
cost, rather than a claim that Vietnamese requests only core bytes.

Preloads retain their original route scope: the web root preloads Noto Sans
Latin and Vietnamese core, marketing adds its display weights and mono core,
and branding adds Inter core. Extended files are never preloaded. All faces
precede their fallback family; no fallback face is inserted between core and
extended. Public files under `/fonts/subsets/` bypass the web proxy so font
requests do not redirect to login.

## Manual regeneration

No font processing runs during install, development, CI or release builds.
Install tools into a disposable environment, then run from the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m venv /tmp/web-font-tools
/tmp/web-font-tools/bin/pip install 'fonttools[woff]==4.60.1' 'brotli==1.1.0'
/tmp/web-font-tools/bin/python scripts/fonts/subset_web_fonts.py
/tmp/web-font-tools/bin/python -m unittest discover -s scripts/fonts -p 'test_*.py'
bun check:changed
```

Admit commands through the executing host's `ttr resources run`. Do not build on
the M4. Other-host dependency builds require the current task's authorization.
The generator uses the repository's pinned Biome formatter; install repository
dependencies first.

Google Fonts TTF sources, served WOFF2 sources and existing Colab Noto Sans
assets are pinned by immutable revision or URL plus SHA-256. JetBrains Mono's
existing local source is hash-checked. Inputs cache outside the repository.
Commit output WOFF2 files, licenses, CSS and manifest. Rerun after intentional
source, character, axis, feature or fallback-metric changes. Review source hashes
and licenses before updating pins.

The public census includes body weights 400–700, display 600/800 and mono
400/700. Four existing display weights remain available for other marketing
routes. Noto Sans retains 100–900 for dashboard and public content. Width is
fixed at Noto Sans's original default 100 and Inter optical size at 14. Inter's
CSS exposes the used 400–700 range; its underlying weight variation data and
JetBrains Mono's original variation data are preserved where trimming changes
browser pixels. This retains extra bytes to preserve appearance.

Default shaping and numeric behavior must survive feature pruning. Preserve
original glyph names and standard family-name records: changing this metadata
can change native font rendering. JetBrains Mono retains its feature closure, original glyph IDs and font bounds
(empty slots replace unused outlines), and seven-byte `prep` rasterizer-control program; glyph instructions are absent.
Explicit U+2010/U+2011 hyphen mappings preserve Chromium normalization formerly
allowed by Google's broad punctuation ranges. Instancer output is serialized
before subsetting because FontTools otherwise removes empty `gvar` entries that
the subsetter expects to exist.

The manifest records bytes, glyph/character counts, axes, features, hint tables,
glyph-instruction counts and SHA-256 digests. Tests open the actual WOFF2 files,
check Vietnamese coverage in each core pool, validate declared ranges against
real cmaps, verify licensing, and prove that public/dashboard roots share the
same body stack. Original overlapping character groups are intentional.

## Licenses and Reserved Font Names

All four pinned families use SIL OFL 1.1. Their copyright headers declare no
Reserved Font Name, so the subsets retain their original family and PostScript
names. Copyright and license records remain with the fonts, and complete OFL
files ship beside the assets. Recheck this permission on source updates; an RFN
requires appropriate derivative names before shipping.

## Rendering acceptance

Capture cold Chromium at 1440×1000 using identical runtime, source fixture,
viewport, theme and motion settings before and after. Await fonts, record font
response-body bytes and preload URLs, inspect computed family/weight/style, and
capture full-page images. Keep explicit specimen loads separate from natural
page traffic. Include composed/decomposed Vietnamese accents, code/monospace,
synthetic italic and CJK probes.

An unchanged control pair identifies existing motion variability. Additionally,
compare each family with the exact baseline font data on a frozen page, after
both font sets load, so animation changes cannot hide font regressions. Do not
accept unexplained text or layout differences.

Report `next dev` response bytes as development measurements, identify overlay
font requests, and give committed file sizes separately. These measurements do
not certify production cache behavior, preload discovery or a release build.
Require exact-commit CI and authenticated dashboard acceptance before removing
the pilot's merge hold.
